manuscript_prose.section1_title: Deep Animal Origins, the Ctenophora–Porifera Root Debate & Basement-Membrane Assembly
manuscript_prose.section1_p1: Resolving the deepest divergences of Animalia—whether comb jellies (Ctenophora) or sponges (Porifera) form the sister lineage to all remaining metazoans alongside Placozoa, Cnidaria, and Bilateria—requires mitigating severe base-composition heterogeneity and rapid mitochondrial evolution across Neoproterozoic divergences.
manuscript_prose.section1_p2: In v4.0.0, all 64 stratified Holozoa and Basal Metazoa slots ([A]-[G]) execute through the generalized declarative bio-suite-supervisor engine with Partitioned ModelTest, empirical Kishino-Hasegawa Z-scores, empirical TimeTreeLSD2 asymmetric 95% HPDs, homogeneous Code-1 Hsp70, FoxJ1, SYT1, and COL4A1 selection models (PDB 1LI1), and 12 real single-species marine skylines.
manuscript_prose.section2_title: Sixteen-Locus Partitioned ModelTest, RY3 De-Biasing & Tonian-to-Ediacaran Holozoa Chronogram
manuscript_prose.section3_title: 64-Species Quartet Multispecies Coalescent & Non-Bilaterian Phylum Concordance
manuscript_prose.section4_title: Purifying Constraint on Hsp70, FoxJ1 Ciliogenesis, Synaptotagmin-1 & Collagen IV NC1 (1LI1)
manuscript_prose.section4_body: Across verified Universal Code 1 metazoan coding orthologs, Goldman-Yang 61-state codon models quantify constraint across thermal stress Hsp70 (FAM-01), ciliogenesis regulator FoxJ1 (FAM-02), synaptic vesicle sensor SYT1 (FAM-03), and basement membrane Type IV collagen COL4A1 (FAM-04) threaded onto PDB 1LI1 (1.90 A).
manuscript_prose.section5_title: Marine Invertebrate Skylines (Slow Anthozoan vs. Pelagic Scyphozoan/Ctenophore mtDNA) & Networks
discussion_paragraphs: **Evaluating the Root of Metazoa Under Compositional De-Biasing.** Few phylogenetic questions have proved as sensitive to substitution modeling as the relative placement of Ctenophora and Porifera at the base of the animal tree [2–7]. While site-heterogeneous CAT-GTR amino-acid reanalyses of selected supermatrices have argued that Ctenophora-sister can arise via long-branch attraction to distant opisthokont outgroups [6, 7], our partitioned RY3 analysis—reducing nucleotide compositional skew by 84.4% (RCFV = 0.0155) while rooting strictly on proximal unicellular Holozoa (*Monosiga*, *Sphaerothecum*, Ichthyosporea)—resolves Holozoa, Porifera, Placozoa, Cnidaria, and Bilateria with 92.3% mean bootstrap support across 48 completeness-gated mitogenomes (100% UFBoot2 on deep backbone nodes) while integrating Ctenophora across 60 multi-locus species via quartet coalescent reconciliation (Q = 0.8005; **Figure 3**). Critically, this framework aligns with model-independent chromosome-scale synteny analyses showing that sponges, cnidarians, and bilaterians share irreversible ancestral linkage-group fusions and rearrangements absent in both ctenophores and unicellular holozoans [2, 11].

**Tonian Divergence Across Cryogenian Glaciations to Ediacaran Macrofossils.** Our relaxed-clock chronology places Crown Metazoa (~839 Ma) and the divergence of Porifera, Placozoa, and Eumetazoa (~783–674 Ma) across the Tonian–Cryogenian transition, followed by Ediacaran crown radiations of Porifera (~643 Ma), Eumetazoa (~619 Ma), and Bilateria (~548 Ma) [14]. These dates reconcile the ~200–250 Myr molecular–paleontological offset between deep stem divergences of soft-bodied microscopic/spicular ancestors and the macroscopic Ediacaran Avalon/White Sea biota (~575–550 Ma) and Fortunian Cambrian trace/skeletal fossils (~539 Ma), as rising Neoproterozoic shelf oxygenation and benthic primary productivity enabled large body sizes and biomineralization [8, 14, 15].

**Structural Entrenchment of Collagen IV Sulfilimine Crosslinks and Synaptic Machinery.** Codon models [19] and structural threading onto PDB 1LI1 [12, 13] illuminate the molecular foundations of animal tissue integrity. Across Porifera (*Pseudocorticium*), Cnidaria (*Hydra*), and Bilateria, *COL4A1* preserves invariant *Gly-X-Y* triplet registers (**Supplemental Figure S1**) and a conserved NC1 fold (TM-score = 0.992; M0 dN/dS = 0.105) framing the Met93–Hyl211 sulfilimine interface [12, 13]. As shown biochemically by Fidler et al. [12], reinforcement of collagen IV scaffolds by peroxidasin-generated hypohalous acid and sulfilimine crosslinks was a mechanical prerequisite for polarized epithelial basement membranes in early metazoans. Equivalently intense purifying constraint on *FoxJ1* (98.0% purifying sites) and *Synaptotagmin-1* (98.6% purifying sites; dN/dS = 0.108) reflects deep conservation of the ancestral holozoan ciliary and SNARE/Ca<sup>2+</sup>-vesicle exocytosis toolkit—even where ctenophores independently co-opted distinct ionotropic receptor and gap-junction repertoires for neural signaling [4, 5, 15].

**Mitochondrial Substitution Stasis in Anthozoans Versus Pelagic Medusozoan and Ctenophore Dispersal.** Our paired multi-locus skylines (**Figure 4B**, **Table 4B**) highlight why single-marker *COX1* barcoding fails at the species level in anthozoan corals yet excels in medusozoans and bilaterians [16]. *Acropora millepora* exhibits zero *COX1* diversity (π = 0.0000) alongside normal nuclear *Hsp70* polymorphism (π = 0.0606), reflecting active mitochondrial DNA repair in Anthozoa [16], whereas pelagic *Aurelia* medusae and invasive *Mnemiopsis leidyi* accumulate informative *COX1* variation tracking basin-scale expansions (*D* = −1.24 to −1.42) [4].

**Study Limitations.** Three limitations bound this synthesis. First, 48 of the 64 holozoan and metazoan species met the ≥50% multi-locus supermatrix completeness gate, while Ctenophora ([B])—whose ultra-compact ~10–11 kb mitogenomes lack *ATP6*, *ATP8*, and *ND6* and evolve at extreme substitution rates [3, 4]—and fragmented-mtDNA calcisponges/cubozoans are placed via 16-locus quartet coalescent reconciliation (**Figure 3**). Second, partitioned nucleotide/RY3 models do not directly model across-site amino-acid profile mixtures (CAT/C60), which remain valuable complementary tests on hundred-gene nuclear transcriptomes [6, 7]. Finally, Tonian–Cryogenian clock intervals remain sensitive to root maximum bounds in the absence of indisputable pre-Ediacaran animal body fossils [14].
manuscript_prose.abstract_context: Reconstructing the earliest animal divergences across comb jellies, sponges, placozoans, cnidarians, and bilaterians requires overcoming deep compositional saturation while tracking the molecular evolution of basement membranes and neural signaling.
manuscript_prose.executive_summary_lead: evaluates deep animal divergences, collagen selection, and marine demography across Basal Metazoa
manuscript_prose.latex_intro: Sixty-four Holozoa and Metazoa taxa spanning unicellular outgroups [A] through Bilateria [G] are evaluated across 16 loci in Version 4.0.0.
manuscript_prose.abstract_override: The evolutionary emergence of multicellular animals (Metazoa) from unicellular holozoan ancestors during the Neoproterozoic—and whether comb jellies (Ctenophora) or sponges (Porifera) represent the sister phylum to all other animals—remains one of the most intensively debated problems in evolutionary biology. Deep non-bilaterian phylogenetics is severely challenged by extreme lineage-specific evolutionary rate disparities between fast-evolving ctenophores and bilaterians versus extraordinarily slow-evolving sponge and anthozoan mitochondrial genomes, alongside compositional bias. Here, we analyze a 16-locus mitochondrial and nuclear ribosomal/coding supermatrix (16,851 aligned base pairs; 10,213 parsimony-informative sites) across 64 holozoan species spanning Choanoflagellata, Filasterea, and Ichthyosporea outgroups, Ctenophora, Porifera (Hexactinellida, Demospongiae, Homoscleromorpha), Placozoa, Cnidaria (Anthozoa, Medusozoa), and Bilateria. Partitioned BIC model selection and third-codon RY3 recoding reduced compositional heterogeneity by 84.4% (RCFV = 0.0155 vs. 0.0994 unrecoded and 0.1628 unfiltered; Δln L = +6,069.54), achieving 92.3% mean bootstrap support across 48 completeness-gated (≥50%) taxa and Q = 0.8005 quartet concordance across 3,652,565 gene-tree quartets (2,923,864 satisfied). Relaxed-clock dating places the Holozoa root in the Tonian at 939.3 Ma (95% HPD: 887.6–991.0 Ma), Crown Metazoa at 838.5 Ma (792.4–884.6 Ma), Porifera–ParaHoxozoa at 782.8 Ma (739.8–825.9 Ma), Crown Eumetazoa at 618.7 Ma (584.7–652.7 Ma), and Crown Bilateria in the late Ediacaran at 548.3 Ma (518.1–578.4 Ma). Codon models across 36 deduplicated orthologs of Hsp70, FoxJ1, SYT1, and COL4A1 confirm strong purifying selection (dN/dS = 0.105–0.117; zero BEB sites), while 3D threading onto the Type IV Collagen NC1 crystal structure (PDB 1LI1; TM-score = 0.992) preserves the Met93–Hyl211 sulfilimine crosslink.
section1_paragraphs: The transition from unicellular and transiently colonial holozoan protists (Choanoflagellata, Filasterea, and Ichthyosporea) to animals (Crown Metazoa) entailed fundamental innovations in polarized epithelia, extracellular matrix scaffolding, motile multiciliogenesis, and fast synaptic signaling [2, 8–12, 15]. At the center of early animal macroevolution lies the unresolved topological conflict between two competing hypotheses for the sister group to all other animals: the classical "Porifera-sister" hypothesis, which interprets collar-flagellate choanocytes as homologous to choanoflagellates and favors a single origin of neurons and muscles in Eumetazoa [6–8, 15], versus the "Ctenophora-sister" hypothesis, supported by multiple phylogenomic matrices, ctenophore genome assemblies (*Mnemiopsis leidyi*, *Pleurobrachia bachei*), and irreversible ancient chromosome-scale gene-linkage (synteny) fusions shared exclusively between sponges, cnidarians, and bilaterians to the exclusion of ctenophores [2–5, 11]. Resolving this root—together with the Neoproterozoic Cryogenian–Ediacaran timeline predating the Cambrian explosion [14]—shapes how we reconstruct the origin of nervous systems, through-guts, and basement membranes.

Non-bilaterian sequence evolution presents extreme substitution-rate and compositional disparities across compartments [3, 6, 7, 16]. Whereas ctenophores possess compact, rapidly evolving mitochondrial genomes and accelerated nuclear substitution rates, demosponges, placozoans (*Trichoplax adhaerens*), and anthozoan cnidarians exhibit some of the slowest mitochondrial nucleotide substitution rates in eukaryotes—associated in octocorals with a horizontally acquired mitochondrial *mtMutS* mismatch-repair gene—contrasted against faster linear mitochondrial chromosomes in medusozoan cnidarians (*Aurelia*, *Hydra*) [9, 10, 16]. Under unpartitioned four-state models, this >10-fold rate asymmetry and compositional drift induce severe systematic bias unless mitigated by per-locus rate multipliers and purine–pyrimidine recoding [3, 6, 7, 14].

Here, we analyze 352 curated holozoan and metazoan sequence records across 64 species (after automated sequence hygiene quarantined 3,419 partial, chimeric, or misannotated GenBank deposits) spanning 16 mitochondrial and nuclear rDNA/coding partitions [1–3, 16]. We integrate edge-linked per-locus BIC model selection and third-codon RY3 recoding with Neoproterozoic–Phanerozoic relaxed-clock dating [14], 64-species quartet multispecies coalescent reconciliation [17], and four-taxon Patterson's *D* tests, paired with 61-state Goldman–Yang codon selection [19] across *Hsp70*, multiciliogenesis master regulator *FoxJ1*, synaptic vesicle Ca<sup>2+</sup> sensor *Synaptotagmin-1* (*SYT1*) [4, 5], and basement-membrane Type IV collagen (*COL4A1*) threaded onto the 1.90 Å crystal structure of the collagen IV NC1 hexamer interface (PDB 1LI1) [12, 13], plus 12 marine invertebrate coalescent skylines and *COX1* networks [16, 18].
section2_paragraphs: Automated homology curation and genetic-code-aware translation across all 64 holozoan and metazoan species assembled a 16-partition supermatrix of 16,851 aligned base pairs containing 10,213 parsimony-informative RY3 sites [1, 16]. Per-locus BIC model selection with proportional rate multipliers and third-codon RY3 recoding reduced relative composition frequency variability by 84.4%—from RCFV = 0.0994 under unrecoded four-state nucleotides and 0.1628 in unfiltered controls to RCFV = 0.0155—and improved marginal log-likelihood by Δln L = +6,069.54 units (ln L = −279,944.86 vs. −286,014.40 unpartitioned; ΔBIC = −10,698.7) across 48 multi-locus reference genomes spanning Holozoa, Porifera, Placozoa, Cnidaria, and Bilateria above the ≥50% sector-balanced completeness gate (**Figures 1 & 2**; **Tables 3A, 3C & 3D**). Mean ultrafast bootstrap support reached 92.3% (100.0% UFBoot2 on basal Holozoa, Metazoa, Benthozoa, and Bilateria backbone splits), compared with 84.6% for single-locus markers.

Rooted on unicellular Holozoa outgroups ([A], *Monosiga brevicollis*, *Sphaerothecum destruens*), the partitioned RY3 phylogeny and constrained relaxed-clock timetree [2–5, 11, 14] place the Holozoa–Metazoa stem divergence (**Node I**) in the Tonian Neoproterozoic at 939.3 Ma (95% HPD: 887.6–991.0 Ma) and Crown Metazoa (**Node II**) at 838.5 Ma (792.4–884.6 Ma) [2, 14]. Within Benthozoa, Porifera ([C]) diverges from ParaHoxozoa in the late Tonian (**Node III**: 782.8 Ma; 739.8–825.9 Ma), followed during the Cryogenian by the ParaHoxozoa split between Placozoa ([D]) and Eumetazoa (**Node V**: 673.5 Ma; 636.4–710.5 Ma) [8–10]. Across the Marinoan–Ediacaran transition, Crown Porifera (**Node IV**: 643.4 Ma; 608.0–678.8 Ma), Crown Eumetazoa separating Cnidaria ([E]–[F]) from Bilateria ([G]) (**Node VI**: 618.7 Ma; 584.7–652.7 Ma), Crown Cnidaria separating Anthozoa from Medusozoa (**Node VII**: 603.4 Ma; 570.2–636.6 Ma), and Crown Bilateria / Nephrozoa (**Node VIII**: 548.3 Ma; 518.1–578.4 Ma; **Figure 1**; **Table 2A**) radiate prior to macroscopic Ediacaran communities [10, 14].
section3_paragraphs: To integrate all 64 holozoan and non-bilaterian species—including glass sponges, calcisponges, ctenophores, and hydrozoans lacking complete nuclear/mitochondrial overlap—we reconciled individual maximum-likelihood gene trees across all 16 partitions under the quartet multispecies coalescent [1, 17]. Across 3,652,565 evaluated four-taxon quartets, the species tree satisfied 2,923,864 quartets, yielding normalized concordance Q = 0.8005 and mean local posterior probability LPP = 0.8800 (**Figure 3**; **Figure 6**; **Table 3A & 2B**).

Four-taxon Patterson's *D* tests (**Table 2B**) reveal symmetric site sharing consistent with incomplete lineage sorting rather than cross-phylum chimerism across deep non-bilaterian splits: Ctenophora/Holozoa vs. Porifera and Cnidaria (ABBA-1: *D* = −0.0420, *Z* = 0.46), Hexacorallia/Octocorallia vs. Scyphozoa (ABBA-3: *D* = +0.0289, *Z* = 0.56), and Medusozoa (ABBA-4: *D* = 0.0000, *Z* = 0.00), with modest rate-driven site asymmetry between slow-evolving Placozoa/Anthozoa and fast-evolving Bilateria (ABBA-2: *D* = +0.1722, *Z* = 3.13) [16].
section4_paragraphs: Fitting 61-state Goldman–Yang codon substitution models [19] across 36 species-deduplicated metazoan coding orthologs aligned with 20-state BLOSUM62 L-INS-i consistency demonstrates uniformly strong purifying selection across all four multicellularity, ciliary, synaptic, and extracellular-matrix gene families (BEB Pr ≥ 0.95 = 0 sites across all families; **Figure 5A–B**; **Table 4A**). Tightest evolutionary conservation across sites governs the synaptic-vesicle exocytosis Ca<sup>2+</sup> sensor *Synaptotagmin-1* (*SYT1*, FAM-03; N = 8 species, 418 codons, M0 dN/dS = 0.1080, κ = 1.41; 98.6% of C2A/C2B Ca<sup>2+</sup>-binding codons at ω<sub>0</sub> = 0.0661) [4, 5] and the forkhead transcription factor *FoxJ1*, master regulator of motile 9+2 cilia from choanoflagellates and sponge choanocytes to ctenophore comb plates and vertebrate airways (FAM-02; N = 12 species, 421 codons, M0 dN/dS = 0.1169, κ = 2.88; 98.0% of sites at ω<sub>0</sub> = 0.0941). Heat-shock chaperone *Hsp70* (FAM-01; N = 8 species, 572 codons, M0 dN/dS = 0.1106, κ = 1.58; 92.3% at ω<sub>0</sub> = 0.0872) and basement-membrane Type IV collagen α-chain *COL4A1* (FAM-04; N = 8 species spanning Porifera *Pseudocorticium*, Cnidaria *Hydra*, Ecdysozoa, and Vertebrata, 480 codons, M0 dN/dS = 0.1045, κ = 0.80; **Supplemental Figure S1**) likewise evolve under strict purifying constraint preserving periodic *Gly-X-Y* triple-helical repeats and the C-terminal non-collagenous NC1 trimerization/hexamerization domain [12, 13].

Three-dimensional homology threading of metazoan *COL4A1* onto the 1.90 Å crystal structure of the Type IV Collagen NC1 domain (PDB 1LI1 Chain A) [13] recovers near-identical β-sheet/subdomain architecture (TM-score = 0.9920; interface cavity 107.6 Å<sup>3</sup>; **Figure 5D**). Sequence-to-structure mapping confirms conservation of the six intrachain disulfide bridges alongside the opposing Met93 and hydroxylysine/lysine-211 (Hyl211) residues that form the peroxidasin-catalyzed covalent sulfilimine bond (–S=N–), mechanically locking collagen IV networks to withstand tissue tensile forces across Eumetazoa and homoscleromorph/demosponge scaffolds [12, 13].
section5_paragraphs: Twelve Bayesian coalescent skylines (25,000 MCMC generations, 20% burn-in) provide a direct empirical demonstration of the mitochondrial substitution-rate paradox across non-bilaterian marine phyla (**Figures 4A & 4B**; **Table 4B**) [1, 16, 18]. Along Axis A (R1–R6, *COX1*), pelagic moon jellies *Aurelia coerulea* (R1, N = 36, π = 0.0071, Tajima's *D* = −1.24) and *A. aurita* (R2, N = 36, π = 0.0044, *D* = −0.26), circumboreal plumose sea anemone *Metridium senile* (R3, N = 36, π = 0.0028, *D* = −2.60), and invasive ctenophore *Mnemiopsis leidyi* (R4, N = 20, π = 0.0087, *D* = −1.42) [4] exhibit post-glacial or trans-oceanic expansion signatures, mirrored in Indo-Pacific scleractinian corals *Pocillopora damicornis* (R5, *D* = −1.93) and *Stylophora pistillata* (R6, *D* = −0.58). Axis B (L1–L6) directly illustrates anthozoan mitochondrial stasis [16]: in staghorn coral *Acropora millepora*, mitochondrial *COX1* displays zero intraspecific polymorphism across 415 bp (L1, N = 12, π = 0.0000), whereas nuclear *Hsp70* coding sequences in the exact same species harbor rich standing variation (L3, N = 10, 649 bp, π = 0.0606, *D* = +0.01), paralleled by nuclear rDNA ITS/28S across *Aurelia* (L2, π = 0.1268) and *Acropora* (L5, π = 0.0655), linear mtDNA in *Hydra vulgaris* (L4, π = 0.0262, *D* = −1.45), and nuclear actin CDS across Actiniaria (L6, N = 12, 1,143 bp, *D* = +1.45).

Minimum-spanning and TCS *COX1* haplotype networks (**Figures 7A & 7B**; **Table 4C**) partition 86 coastal *Aurelia* scyphozoan sequences into 29 geographic species/cryptic clusters (Panel A, 57 haplotypes across 534 bp, *H*<sub>d</sub> = 0.9598) and 98 Anthozoa and Hydrozoa sequences into 50 deeply diverged clusters reflecting strong inter-genus structure (Panel B, 57 haplotypes across 549 bp, *H*<sub>d</sub> = 0.9236; **Table 4C**).
